chunks: And it is narrated from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“Write for the runaway slave on a piece of paper or on parchment: ‘In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.’”
“The hand of so-and-so is bound to his neck; when he brings it out, he can hardly see it. And whomever Allah has not made a light for, for him there is no light.”
Then wrap it, then place it between two sticks, then cast it into a dark niche of the house in the place where he used to stay.

key_terms.كُوَّةِ: a niche or opening in a house
key_terms.نُورًا: light, meaning divine guidance or illumination in context

ai.seo_question: What should be written for an absconding slave according to a narration from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs a written formula to be used concerning an absconding slave, including a Qur'anic phrase about darkness and the absence of divine light. It reflects a practical directive transmitted in the hadith corpus and incorporates Qur'anic wording as part of the prescribed text.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3544 - Abu Jameelah narrated from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdullah (as):
"Write for the runaway slave on a piece of paper or parchment: 'In the Name of Allah (swt), the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
The hand of [slave's name] is tied to his neck. If he extends it, he will hardly see it. And whomever Allah (swt) has not granted light, for him there is no light (Surah An-Nur 24:40).'
Then wrap it, place it between two sticks, and throw it into a dark corner of the house where he used to stay."
